objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed promotion admission that requires source lineage, finality threshold, explicit conflict disposition, identity and scope binding, generation and expiry fences, replay/tamper protection, and non-authority boundaries before a memory candidate can be considered promotion-eligible.

research_inputs.finding: Computer-use execution should be isolated, high-impact actions should retain human oversight, and screenshots, page text, tool outputs, PDFs, emails, chats, and third-party content are untrusted input.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Promotion receipts do not authorize tools, browser actions, external effects, or policy changes.

research_inputs.finding: Evidence tracing should connect tools, memory, observations, claims, actions, and agent interactions for verification, safety, audit, and recovery.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Promotion binds candidate digest, source lineage digest/count, finality receipt, conflict disposition, principal, tenant, subject scope, generation, and expiry.

research_inputs.finding: Invocation-bound authorization should combine identity, attenuated scope, and provenance in an append-only chain.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Promotion requests are bound to principal, tenant, requested scope, candidate lineage, policy generation, and nonce replay protection.

research_inputs.finding: Per-agent behavior and per-memory provenance are relevant defenses against memory poisoning in multi-agent systems.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Unresolved conflict, insufficient finality, identity mismatch, scope mismatch, stale generation, and expiry fail closed; local promotion never claims truth.

features: candidate lineage digest and bounded lineage count

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane receipt overhead; excludes actual memory persistence, retrieval, model inference, network, accelerator, and kernel scheduling latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the memory-promotion module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged task-routing release

limitations: Promotion admission does not write memory or make a candidate true; a separate trusted memory service must enforce the receipt.
Finality counts, conflict dispositions, lineage digests, and identity claims are caller-supplied evidence and require independent trusted collection for production use.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes actual storage, retrieval, distributed consensus, model, network, accelerator, and kernel scheduler performance.
The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish memory quality, general intelligence, browser autonomy, robotics, or production agent efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
